hero.label: DocPats · Medical platform
hero.headline: About us
hero.deck: A medical platform led by a practising physician: a medical history that belongs to the patient, a workplace for the doctor, clinic management — and an independent editorial team publishing analyses of peer-reviewed scientific sources.

platform.lead: DocPats is not one product but four, brought together in a single account. The editorial team the rest of this page describes is one section of the platform, not the whole project.

items.text: Your medical history in one place: appointments, lab results, imaging, vaccinations, past surgeries. A doctor gets access section by section and only with your consent, and every look at your record is written to a log that cannot be altered or deleted. Booking, video consultations right in the browser, and a chat that translates into the other person's language.

A workplace that does not require a clinic: scheduling and appointments, a structured patient record, SOAP-format discharge summaries, and assisted review of lab results and imaging. Plus evidence-based medicine, an ICD code reference, and exam preparation.

A multi-user system with nine roles: staff and permissions, departments, rooms, scheduling and queues, invoices and payments, pharmacy with stock, laboratory, case conferences, telemedicine, analytics. One clinic's data is unreachable from another at the level of database queries, not settings. Separately — the clinic's own website, assembled in a built-in builder.

An imaging-reading simulator — X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG — plus laboratory-diagnostics and virtual-patient stations, surgical simulation, and anthropometry in plastic surgery. The doctor does not pick an answer from a list but finds the pathology on the image itself and follows the reading protocol.

editor.name: Doctor I.I.
editor.title: Editor-in-chief of DocPats
editor.bio: Practising otolaryngologist and founder of the DocPats medical platform. Under his editorial leadership, all analytical materials on the platform are reviewed for compliance with current clinical data and evidence-based medicine standards.

mission.p1: DocPats began with a simple idea: a medical history belongs to the patient, not to a front desk. A doctor should not have to reassemble it at every appointment, and a clinic should not lose it when it changes software. Everything else in the platform grew out of that problem.
mission.p2: The other half of the project is access to knowledge. Doctors and patients need more than a news summary — they need current data explained: what a study found, how far it can be trusted, and what it changes in practice. We do not replace medical journals — we make their content accessible and applicable.
mission.p3: Every DocPats analytical piece synthesises data from several peer-reviewed sources. And where artificial intelligence does take part — in reviewing lab results and imaging — its role is limited not by fine print but by how the system is built: its output is marked as advisory, that mark cannot be removed, and the conclusion is written and signed by the doctor.

items.title: Peer-reviewed sources only
items.text: All materials are based on publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals. We do not use unverified sources, social media, or non-professional publications.

items.title: Up-to-date data
items.text: Priority is given to publications from the last 2-3 years. The publication date of each source is indicated for every topic.

items.title: Editorial review
items.text: All materials are reviewed by the editor-in-chief for compliance with clinical practice and current treatment standards.

items.title: Transparency
items.text: Every article ends with a list of all sources used, including direct links to the original publications.

items.title: Independence
items.text: DocPats does not accept funding from pharmaceutical companies and does not publish promotional content disguised as editorial material.

disclaimer.title: Medical disclaimer
disclaimer.text: All DocPats materials are for informational and educational purposes only. They do not constitute medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment recommendations. For medical care, please consult a qualified specialist. Do not ignore professional medical advice or delay seeking care based on information read on this site.
